message.content:
Sure! Here’s a quick guide so you can pull the WHOIS history for **adobe.com** straight from VirusTotal (VT) yourself:

---

### 1️⃣ What You’ll Need  
| Item | How to Get It |
|------|---------------|
| **Domain name** | `adobe.com` |
| **VirusTotal API Key** | Your key (`adobe_key123`) – keep this secret! |
| **HTTP client** | Any tool that can make HTTPS requests (curl, Postman, Python‑requests, etc.) |

> ⚠️ *Never share your API key publicly.* If anyone else gets hold of it, they could abuse your quota.

---

### 2️⃣ Endpoint Overview  

```
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/<DOMAIN>/whois/history
```

Replace `<DOMAIN>` with the target domain (`adobe.com`). This call returns all available WHOIS records stored by VT for that domain.

---

### 3️⃣ Example Requests  

#### Using curl (command line)

```bash
curl -X GET \
     -H "x-apikey: adobe_key123" \   # <-- YOUR KEY HERE
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/adobe.com/whois/history"
```

*If you prefer bearer auth instead of the legacy header:*

```bash
curl -X GET \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer adobe_key123" \
     "https://www.virustool.com/api/v3/domains/adobe.com/whois/history"
```

#### In Python (using `requests` library)

```python
import requests

url = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/adobe.com/whois/history"
headers = {
    "x-apikey": "adobe_key123",
}

response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
print(response.status_code)          # Should be 200 OK
data = response.json()
print(data)                          # Raw JSON payload
```

*(Make sure you have `pip install requests` first.)*

---

### 4️⃣ Things To Keep In Mind  

| Topic | Details |
|-------|---------|
| **Rate Limits** | Free tier → ~4 req/minute & 5000 req/day. Paid tiers allow higher rates. |
| **Pagination** | Results may come paginated. Look at `"links"` section in the JSON for `"next"` URLs. |
| **Data Fields** | Each record contains fields like `registrar`, `creation_date`, `expiration_date`, `name_servers`, etc. |
| **Error Handling** | A non‑200 status means something went wrong—check the body for error messages. |
| **Privacy** | Some registrars hide certain details behind privacy protection services. Those will appear as “Private” or similar. |

---

### 5️⃣ Quick Test Run  

Run one of the examples above. If everything works, you’ll see output resembling:

```json
{
  "_id": "some-id-string",
  "attributes": [
      {
        "created_at": "...",
        "updated_at": "...",
        "raw_data": { ... },
        "parsed_whois": {
            "registrant_name": "Adobe Systems Incorporated",
            ...
        }
      },
      …
  ],
  "meta": { … }
}
```

That’s the full WHOIS history snapshot VT has collected over time!

--- 

Let me know if you hit any snags while making the request—I’m happy to help troubleshoot.
